Alkyoneus is a boss in Xenosaga: Pied Piper. This is the last of 7 bosses leading up to the final boss of the game. This is the only enemy in the game with a weakness to Air. This means that 's and 's Shutter Soul and Icicle Sword are effective against it. It has strong party-wide attacks, though, and one of them is designed to reduce characters' ether attack and defense.

is a track in Xenosaga II to III: A Missing Year. Despite its name, it is unrelated to and . Armu rearing is a series of tasks in Xenoblade Chronicles 3, in which the party helps Tussore raise and breed Armus and Arduns for Colony Mu. It unlocks after completing The Future I Want to Spin. Armu rearing involves raising successive generations of Armu and Ardun from infancy, then choosing which ones to pair up in order to breed the next generation. Each choice is made from a selection of four: all possible pairings of an Armu and Ardun from a selection of two Armu and two Ardun. The available "set" of choices is determined by the choice made in the previous generation; see the image at the top of the page for which sets lead to which choices. Auto dialogues, autotalk in the code, are dialogues between non-talkable s in Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and Torna ~ The Golden Country. They happen automatically when the party is at a close enough distance from them on the field. Auto dialogues do not interrupt gameplay like regular dialogue, with the player being able to walk, start battle and talk to NPCs as usual. These dialogues serve as a way to give insight into the daily lives of Alrest's inhabitants, make cities feel more lively, as well as to give bits of lore about a certain item, NPC or character. Audhumla is an boss in Xenosaga: Pied Piper. This enemy is fought at the end of the Virtual Space Cathedral at Point NG-PP6-42T8. It is the second boss in the game. It mainly fires strong beam attacks, and can buff its own evasion or reduce the physical defense of a party member.

Bandai Namco Entertainment Inc. (formerly Namco Bandai Holdings and Bandai Namco Games Inc.) is a Japanese video game developer and publisher formed as a merger between Namco Ltd. and Bandai Co., Ltd.. The company was responsible for publishing the final Xenosaga game, Xenosaga Episode III - Also Sprach Zarathustra, prior to Monolith Soft's sale to Nintendo in 2007. Additionally, they are credited as one of the developers of the 2026 release of Xenosaga: Pied Piper together with G-MODE.

Some situations have multiple potential voicelines, only one of which is chosen (assumed to be at random).

Battle Commands are actions in the of Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are accessed via the Battle Menu, which can be opened in combat by pressing +. There are three main components to the Battle Menu. The first is a submenu from which any combat-related Consumable Items may be used: Personal Patch, Fuel Re-up, Frame Patch, Tensifier, or Mega Tensifier. The second, "Issue Orders", is a series of lists by which the player may partially manipulate the -controlled party members. These orders include commands such as to enter or exit Skells, to use melee or ranged attacks, and to attack a specific targeted appendage. The Booster Probe G1 is a Data Probe in Xenoblade Chronicles X. When placed, a Booster Probe G1 boosts the effect of probes in FN Sites connected to the probe's site, multiplying each effect by 1.5 (150%). However, it doesn't boost other booster probes and its effects cannot be chained.

The Booster Probe G2 is a Data Probe in Xenoblade Chronicles X. When placed, a Booster Probe G2 boosts the effect of probes in FN Sites connected to the probe's site, multiplying each effect by 2 (200%). However, it doesn't boost other booster probes and its effects cannot be chained.
